title: My Recipes vs All Recipes toggle (shared family visibility)
description: Let any approved family member browse everyone's recipes ('All Recipes'), not just their own ('My Recipes' - today's only view). This is a real architecture shift: recipes/tags/recipe_tags RLS currently restricts SELECT to user_id = auth.uid() only (migration 001) - every approved user's SELECT needs to open up to all rows, while INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE stay scoped to the owning user_id (you can browse everyone's recipes but only edit/delete your own).
design:
RLS changes needed (recipes, tags, recipe_tags - migration 001's policies): SELECT policy changes from 'user_id = auth.uid()' to something like 'EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM profiles WHERE id = auth.uid() AND approval_status = ''approved'')' (i.e. gated by approval, not ownership) - depends on recipes-b28's admin-approval issue landing first, or at minimum landing together, since opening full visibility to any Google account with no approval gate would be a real problem.

Storage: the recipe-photos bucket's RLS (migration 002) currently gates read access by {user_id} folder prefix matching auth.uid() - meaning today, User A literally cannot load User B's photos even if the recipes table SELECT opens up. That policy needs the same loosening (any approved user can read any recipe-photos object; INSERT/DELETE stay scoped to own folder).

Tags: currently user-scoped (tags.user_id) too - each user has their own private tag vocabulary. Once recipes are shared, does 'All Recipes' browse by a shared/merged tag list, or does the tag filter only ever show the viewer's own tags regardless of whose recipes are displayed? Needs a decision - probably tags should become shared/global (drop user_id scoping, or keep it as 'created by' metadata but let anyone use any tag for filtering) since per-user tag silos don't make sense once recipes themselves are shared.

UI: app.html needs a My Recipes / All Recipes toggle (tabs or a switch) driving the recipes query's filter; search recipes-022.4 (search/categories, still open) - that work should build against whichever scope is active.
acceptance_criteria: Toggling to 'All Recipes' shows recipes added by every approved family member, including their photos. 'My Recipes' shows only the signed-in user's own. Editing/deleting someone else's recipe is still blocked. An unapproved/unauthenticated user sees neither view.
close_reason:
Built and verified 2026-08-27. Migration 007: opened SELECT on recipes/tags/recipe_tags and the recipe-photos storage bucket to any approved user (was owner-only), while INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on recipes stay owner-scoped - browse everyone's, edit only your own. Also resolved this issue's own open design question: tags became a fully shared family vocabulary (dropped per-user UNIQUE(user_id, name) in favor of UNIQUE(name), merged any cross-user name collisions first) rather than staying siloed per-user, since a shared 'All Recipes' view with per-user tag chips would've been incoherent (two separate 'dinner' chips, one per user). No client-side tag rename/delete existed before this and none was added - only service_role can modify a shared tag now.

app.html gained a My Recipes / All Recipes toggle (defaults to My Recipes) driving the recipes query's user_id filter; tags/recipe_tags queries are always unfiltered now. add-recipe.html's findOrCreateTags() matches against all tags, not just the current user's own.

Verified via direct API calls: an approved user (Pete) can SELECT a recipe owned by a different approved user (Samantha, via a temporary test row) but a DELETE attempt on it returns 0 rows affected - write protection intact. Verified the toggle in-browser: switching to All Recipes updates the breadcrumb and re-queries correctly, no console errors.

title: Admin approval gate for new signups
description: Pete (as admin) should approve new users before they get access, rather than any Google account being able to sign in and immediately see/add family recipes (which is the current behavior since recipes-adi made Google sign-in the only entry point with no invite gate). Mirror the pattern already used by the sibling project Five Wonders (same repo family, github.com/docneville/five-wonders), which has exactly this: profiles.approval_status ('pending'|'approved'|'rejected'|'suspended') and profiles.is_admin (boolean), defaulting new signups to pending/not-admin, with index.html branching on status to show the app vs. a 'waiting for approval'/'not approved' message.
design:
Reference implementation to mirror: five-wonders/index.html lines ~119-160 (profile fetch, default-to-pending insert on first sign-in, status branching) - see [five-wonders/index.html](https://github.com/docneville/five-wonders/blob/main/index.html). One deliberate deviation: Five Wonders enforces approval_status inside its Edge Functions (manage-places, manage-lists - see supabase/functions/manage-places/index.ts's getApprovedUserId()) because all its writes go through Edge Functions. Recipes has no CRUD edge functions - the client talks to recipes/tags/recipe_tags directly via RLS - so enforcement belongs in RLS policies instead: every INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policy on recipes, tags, and recipe_tags needs an added check like EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM profiles WHERE id = auth.uid() AND approval_status = 'approved'), and the same for the recipe-photos storage bucket's INSERT policy. This is stronger than Five Wonders' approach (can't be bypassed by a future page that talks to the tables directly and forgets the check).

Migration: add approval_status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' CHECK (...) and is_admin BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false to the existing profiles table (migration 003_create_profiles.sql already exists - this is a new migration). Pete's own row needs to be manually set to approved + is_admin=true after migration (there's exactly one real user right now, pmorse@gmail.com / fbaa2a56-05bc-4dfc-8a82-bc62b01aa390).

UI: index.html's signed-in branch needs to check approval_status same as Five Wonders - pending shows a waiting message, rejected/suspended shows the corresponding message, only approved shows the normal Welcome/Your recipes view.

Open question for Pete: does he want an in-app admin approval UI (a page listing pending users with approve/reject buttons), or is manual approval via the Supabase dashboard table editor fine for now, same as Five Wonders currently does (grepped - no in-app admin UI exists there either, it's dashboard-only)? Given family-scale volume this is probably fine to punt on an admin UI initially, but confirm.
acceptance_criteria: A brand-new Google sign-in lands in 'pending' status and sees a waiting-for-approval message instead of the recipe app. After Pete flips their profiles.approval_status to 'approved' (via dashboard or a future admin UI), they can sign in normally and their writes to recipes/tags succeed. An unapproved user's direct Supabase client calls to insert/update recipes fail at the RLS level even if they bypass the UI.
close_reason:
Built and verified 2026-08-27. Migration 006 adds profiles.approval_status ('pending'|'approved'|'rejected'|'suspended', default pending) and is_admin (default false), mirroring Five Wonders' pattern but enforced via RLS (not Edge Functions, since Recipes has none) - INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on recipes/tags/recipe_tags and INSERT/DELETE on the recipe-photos storage bucket all now require an is_approved() check. Also closed a privilege-escalation gap found while building this: the existing profiles UPDATE policy only restricted which row a user could touch, not which columns, so any signed-in user could have self-approved via a direct API call - fixed with column-level GRANTs restricting the authenticated role to first_name/last_name/avatar_url only, verified a self-escalation attempt now gets 42501 permission denied.

index.html now branches on approval_status after sign-in: pending shows a waiting-for-approval message, rejected/suspended show their own message, only approved shows the normal welcome/recipes UI. Verified end-to-end: pending user sees the waiting message and a direct API insert attempt is blocked by RLS; approved user sees the normal UI and inserts/deletes work with no regression.

Manually approved the two real accounts: Pete (pmorse@gmail.com, also set is_admin=true) and his wife Samantha (samanthasmith@gmail.com, who had already signed up) - no in-app admin UI was built (matches Five Wonders' own precedent, which is dashboard-only too), so future approvals are manual via the Supabase dashboard or asking me to flip the row, until/unless an admin UI gets its own issue.

title: Recipes v3: family sharing, admin approval, navigation
description: Pete's requests (2026-08-25) push Recipes from a personal recipe box toward a shared family app: anyone in the Morse family can see everyone's recipes, new signups need admin approval before they get access, recipes show who added them, and any recipe can be shared publicly via a link that works without an account. Plus two navigation asks (breadcrumbs, hamburger menu). Filed as 6 child issues - see recipes-022's own remaining items (022.3 finished-dish photos, 022.4 search/categories) for the personal-recipe-box-era backlog this epic partially supersedes/extends.
close_reason: All 7 children shipped and verified: admin approval gate (b28.1), My/All Recipes shared visibility (b28.2), recipe attribution (b28.3), public share links (b28.4), family-significance field (b28.7), breadcrumbs (b28.5), hamburger menu (b28.6). Recipes is now a working shared family app with an approval gate protecting it.

title: AI photo-to-recipe import (core feature)
description: The core reason this app exists: let Pete snap/upload one or more photos of a recipe (a cookbook page, a handwritten card, a series of screenshots from a Pinterest pin or a blog post) and have Claude read them and turn them into a clean, structured, ad-free recipe - title, ingredients, steps, timing/servings if visible - ready to review and save. This replaces screenshotting/bookmarking recipes on ad-laden sites like Pinterest just to reference them later.
design: New page (e.g. import.html) - user selects 1+ images, they upload to a private storage path (new bucket 'recipe-imports' or a subpath of existing 'recipe-photos', {user_id}/... gated same as migration 002), then a Supabase Edge Function sends the image(s) to Claude (vision) with a tool-schema prompt asking for {title, description, prep_minutes, cook_minutes, servings, ingredients: [{quantity,unit,name}], instructions: [string], source_name, source_url} matching the recipes table shape exactly, so the result can prefill add-recipe.html's form fields directly for review/edit before saving (never auto-saved - user always confirms). Mirrors Houstory's upload.html -> analyze-media edge function pattern (houstory-96t.2/.3), but returns the recipes schema instead of a freeform description. Multi-image input matters - a single recipe is often 2-4 screenshots stitched together (intro, ingredients, steps).
acceptance_criteria: Can select 2-3 photos of a real recipe (e.g. a Pinterest screenshot series), submit, and get back a structured draft with correct title/ingredients/steps that prefills the add-recipe form for review before saving. Handles a single photo too. Original source photos are stored and remain viewable/attached to the saved recipe.
close_reason: Built and verified end-to-end: import.html uploads photo(s) to recipe-photos/{user_id}/imports/, calls the new extract-recipe edge function (Claude Sonnet 5, forced tool_choice to extract_recipe matching the recipes table shape), result prefills add-recipe.html for review before saving, source photos persist via recipes.source_photo_paths (migration 004) and render on recipe.html. Tested with a synthetic cluttered recipe screenshot (ads/nav/comments included) - Claude correctly extracted only the real recipe content and ignored the clutter. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY secret configured on the Supabase project; function deployed.

title: Recipes v2: AI photo import, Google sign-in, finished-dish photos, richer search
description: Next phase after the v1 core loop (recipes-62x, closed). Pete's stated goal: capture recipes from diverse places (screenshots, photo of a cookbook page, Pinterest pins) so nothing gets lost, without living in an ad-laden site like Pinterest to reference them later. Four workstreams, each filed as its own child issue: Google sign-in, AI-powered photo-to-recipe import (the core differentiator), finished-dish photos, and better search/categories.

title: Recipes v1: personal recipe box core loop
description: Ship the core loop: sign up/sign in, add a recipe (title/ingredients/steps/tags/timing), browse/search/filter your recipe list, view a recipe, edit/delete it. Scaffolded 2026-08-21 mirroring the Five Wonders/Houstory infra pattern (static HTML/CSS/JS, Supabase Postgres+Storage, GitHub Pages, bd).
acceptance_criteria: Can sign up, add a recipe with ingredients+steps+tags, see it in the list, filter by tag, search by title, view detail, edit it, and delete it - all working against the live Supabase project.
close_reason: v1 core loop shipped and verified end-to-end in browser (2026-08-21). Superseded by the v2 epic (recipes-022) for the next phase of work.

title: Show a thumbnail photo on recipe browse/search cards
description: app.html's recipe cards (the My Recipes/All Recipes list) are currently text-only - title, prep/cook time, servings, tags. Add a thumbnail image per card, using the recipe's photo (see recipes-ten for letting the owner pick which one is 'main'; falls back to the first-uploaded photo via recipe_photos.created_at when no main is set, or when recipes-ten hasn't shipped yet - this issue can ship standalone against just that fallback and pick up main_photo_id later without a redesign).
design:
Card rendering is in app.html's render() function (~line 81-100) - currently maps allRecipes to card HTML with no image. loadData() (~line 128-142) would need a fourth query alongside recipes/tags/recipe_tags: one representative photo per recipe (Postgres DISTINCT ON (recipe_id) ... ORDER BY recipe_id, created_at ASC, or once recipes-ten ships, ORDER BY recipe_id, (id = main_photo_id) DESC, created_at ASC so an explicit main photo wins over the first-uploaded fallback).

Performance note: a batch query for one representative photo per visible recipe (not N+1 signed-URL calls) is important once there are many recipes in 'All Recipes' - fetch storage_paths in one query, then Promise.all the createSignedUrl calls same as recipe.html already does for its own photo grid.

Card layout: recipes.css's .rc-recipe-card (~line 215+) currently has no image slot - needs a fixed-size thumbnail (similar sizing to .rc-photo-item's 140x140, probably smaller for a card, e.g. 60-80px) placed alongside/above the title. A recipe with zero photos should show the card as it looks today (no broken image, no empty gap).
acceptance_criteria: Recipes that have at least one photo show a small thumbnail on their browse card (My Recipes and All Recipes both). Recipes with no photos show the card exactly as today, no placeholder/broken image. Performance: doesn't do a separate network round-trip per card.
close_reason: Built and verified 2026-08-30. loadData() (app.html) fetches recipe_photos unfiltered alongside recipes/tags/recipe_tags (same batched, select-all-group-client-side pattern already used for tags), ordered oldest-first per recipe. For each recipe: prefer the photo matching main_photo_id (recipes-ten) if set, else the first-uploaded one, else no thumbnail. Signed URLs are generated in one batched Promise.all for just the recipes that have a resolved photo, not per-card. render() adds the thumbnail (72x72, rc-recipe-thumb) via a has-thumb modifier class that switches the card to a flex layout; recipes with no photos render exactly as before (no broken image, no layout change). Verified in browser: a recipe with a freshly-uploaded test photo correctly showed the thumbnail (confirmed loaded via naturalWidth, not just present in the DOM); recipes with no photos showed no thumb class and no at all. Notably also caught a recipe (Spanish Potato and Spinach Frittata) that already had a real photo from Pete's actual use of the app, and it rendered correctly too - confirmed against real data, not just the test case.

title: Let recipe owner select a 'main' photo from multiple uploads
description: Once a recipe has multiple photos (recipes-022.3: cooking-process shots, finished dish, people eating, whatever), let the owner designate one as the 'main' photo - the one used as a thumbnail when browsing/searching (see the companion issue for that). Without this, thumbnails can only ever default to whichever photo happens to be first-uploaded, which won't always be the best representative one.
design:
Schema choice: recommend recipes.main_photo_id UUID REFERENCES recipe_photos(id) ON DELETE SET NULL (nullable) over a recipe_photos.is_main boolean - a single FK pointer avoids needing a uniqueness constraint/trigger to enforce 'only one photo can be main per recipe', and ON DELETE SET NULL cleanly falls back to 'no main photo' if the designated photo gets deleted. Null means 'no explicit main photo set' - the browsing/thumbnail feature should fall back to first-uploaded (by created_at) in that case, same as before this issue exists.

RLS: updating recipes.main_photo_id is just a normal recipes UPDATE, already scoped to the owner + is_approved() (migration 006) - no new policy needed, just need to make sure main_photo_id is settable via the existing recipe update path (it will be, since recipes UPDATE isn't column-restricted like profiles is).

UI: on recipe.html's photo grid (added in recipes-022.3, ~line 42 area), each photo gets a 'Set as main photo' control visible only to the owner (isRecipeOwner), and the current main photo gets a visual marker (e.g. a star badge or highlighted border) so it's obvious which one is set. Clicking sets recipes.main_photo_id to that photo's id (and probably: clicking the already-main photo's button unsets it back to null/first-uploaded default).
acceptance_criteria: A recipe with 3+ photos lets the owner pick any one as 'main' from the photo grid, with a clear visual indicator of which one is currently selected. A non-owner viewing the same recipe sees the marker but no control to change it. Unsetting (or never setting) falls back to showing the first-uploaded photo as main.
close_reason:
Built and verified 2026-08-30. Migration 012 adds recipes.main_photo_id UUID REFERENCES recipe_photos(id) ON DELETE SET NULL - a single FK pointer rather than a recipe_photos.is_main boolean, avoiding any need for a uniqueness constraint. No new RLS policy needed since setting it is a normal recipes UPDATE, already owner+approved-gated.

recipe.html's photo grid (recipes-022.3) now shows a '★ Main' badge on the designated photo (visible to everyone) and, for the owner, a 'Set as main' / 'Unset as main' toggle button per photo plus the existing Delete button.

Verified end-to-end with two real test photos: setting one as main correctly updated recipes.main_photo_id in the database and showed the badge; unsetting cleared it back to null; deleting the currently-main photo correctly auto-cleared main_photo_id back to null via the FK's ON DELETE SET NULL (verified in the database, not just the UI) rather than leaving a dangling reference.

title: Add a 'why this matters to our family' field to recipes
description: A new field on each recipe capturing why it's meaningful to the family - not a cooking note (that's what recipes.notes already covers - tips, substitutions) but the story/sentiment: whose recipe it originally was, what occasion it's tied to, why it's worth keeping. Fits the whole point of recipes-b28 (family sharing, not just personal storage).
design:
Suggested field label: 'Why This Recipe Matters to Us' (DB column: recipes.significance TEXT, nullable) - open to a better label/phrasing, this is just a starting proposal. Suggested placeholder text to prompt for it: 'Whose recipe is this? What's the story or occasion behind it?'

Schema: simple ALTER TABLE recipes ADD COLUMN significance TEXT; no new table needed, same pattern as the existing notes column.

Placement: add-recipe.html gets a new textarea alongside the existing Notes field, but recipe.html should probably show it prominently - near the top (under the title/description, before the meta/ingredients), styled as a distinct callout rather than blending in with the ingredient list, since it's the emotional/story context that's the actual point of a *family* recipe box vs. a generic one. Once recipes-b28.3 (attribution - 'Added by X') ships, these two probably sit near each other visually (who added it + why it matters).
acceptance_criteria: Can add/edit a 'why this matters' note on a recipe from the add/edit form. It displays prominently on the recipe detail page when present, and is simply absent (no empty section) when a recipe doesn't have one.
close_reason: Built and verified 2026-08-27 with the proposed label as-is (Pete didn't request changes). Migration 009 adds recipes.significance TEXT. add-recipe.html: new textarea labeled 'Why This Recipe Matters to Us' with placeholder 'Whose recipe is this? What's the story or occasion behind it?', wired into save/edit-load same as the existing notes field. recipe.html: displays it prominently between the byline and the meta/ingredients as a distinct callout (left-accent-bordered box, small caps label '💛 Why This Recipe Matters', italicized text), absent entirely when a recipe has none. Verified end-to-end: saved a recipe with a significance value, confirmed it renders correctly on the detail page, confirmed edit mode prefills the textarea from the saved value.

title: Hamburger menu icon overflows its button box
description: The hamburger menu button (nav.js, added in recipes-b28.6) doesn't fit its own box - the ☰ glyph overflows/clips instead of sitting centered inside the 40x40 circle.
design:
Root cause: .rc-hamburger (nav.js's injected <style>, ~line 25-39) sets width:40px/height:40px but never resets padding, so it inherits the global button rule in recipes.css (padding: 0.6rem 1.2rem). Combined with recipes.css's global * { box-sizing: border-box; }, that padding eats almost the entire fixed-size box - left/right padding alone (1.2rem * 2 ≈ 38px) leaves only ~2px of content width for a 1.25rem (~20px) glyph to render in, so it overflows the visible circle instead of being centered.

Fix: add padding: 0 to .rc-hamburger (and ideally display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; for reliable glyph centering regardless of font-size changes, rather than relying on line-height alone).
acceptance_criteria: The ☰ icon renders fully inside its bordered circle on every page, centered, with no clipping or overflow, at both desktop and mobile widths.
close_reason: Fixed: added padding:0 plus display:flex/align-items:center/justify-content:center to .rc-hamburger in nav.js, so the button no longer inherits the global button rule's padding (0.6rem 1.2rem) that was shrinking its content box to ~2px wide inside the fixed 40x40 border-box. Verified via computed styles in browser: padding is now 0px, box stays 40x40, glyph centered.

title: Normalize tag names to lowercase so they consolidate
description: Tags don't consolidate correctly today - 'Dinner', 'dinner', and 'DINNER' are stored as three separate rows since tags.name matching is case-sensitive everywhere it's used. tags has UNIQUE(user_id, name) (migration 001), and add-recipe.html's findOrCreateTags() does an exact-match lookup (.eq('name', name)) before inserting - so any casing difference creates a duplicate tag instead of reusing the existing one, fragmenting the tag filter on app.html and diluting each tag's recipe count.
design:
Two parts:

1. Data fix (migration): normalize all existing tags.name values to lower(name), merging any now-colliding duplicates per user - for each user_id where two tag rows would collide after lowercasing, re-point recipe_tags.tag_id from the duplicate(s) to one canonical surviving row, then delete the duplicate tags rows, then lowercase the survivor's name. Needs to happen in that order (repoint associations before deleting) to avoid orphaning recipe_tags rows or hitting the recipe_tags PK (recipe_id, tag_id) uniqueness constraint - a recipe tagged with both 'Dinner' and 'dinner' should end up tagged with just one merged 'dinner' row, not fail the merge.

2. Enforce going forward at the DB level (not just client-side) so it can't regress: add a BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE trigger on tags that sets NEW.name = lower(trim(NEW.name)), same pattern as the existing touch_updated_at() trigger (migration 001). This is more robust than only fixing add-recipe.html's client-side matching, since it guarantees consolidation regardless of which code path writes a tag.

Also update add-recipe.html's findOrCreateTags() (recipes.html ~line 179-193) to lowercase/trim the name before its .eq('name', name) lookup - the trigger alone would still let the client miss an existing tag and attempt a duplicate insert (which would then fail the UNIQUE constraint after lowercasing, or silently 23505-error) rather than cleanly finding and reusing it; matching client-side first avoids relying on a failed-insert-then-retry path.
acceptance_criteria: Existing duplicate-cased tags in the live data are merged into one lowercase row each, with all their recipes still tagged. Adding a tag with any casing ('Dinner', 'DINNER', 'dinner') on a recipe that already has a differently-cased version of that tag reuses the same tag row rather than creating a new one. The tag filter on app.html never shows two chips that are the same word in different casing.
close_reason: Fixed: migration 005_lowercase_tags.sql merges any existing case-variant duplicate tags per user (re-pointing recipe_tags before dropping the loser), lowercases all tags.name values, and adds a BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE trigger that normalizes name = lower(trim(name)) going forward. add-recipe.html's findOrCreateTags() now also lowercases/trims before its match query. Verified live: inserting a mixed-case tag via the DB comes back normalized; saving a recipe through the actual UI with tags 'DINNER, Quick' correctly reused the existing lowercase 'dinner'/'quick' rows with no new duplicates created.

title: Public share link for a recipe (no account needed to view)
description: A share button on recipe.html that produces a link anyone can open and read the recipe, no sign-in required - for sending a recipe to someone outside the family who doesn't have (and shouldn't need) a Morse Recipes account.
design:
Needs a per-recipe share token: add share_token UUID (nullable, unique, e.g. default gen_random_uuid() so every recipe already has one - simpler than lazily generating on first share click) to recipes. New RLS SELECT policy for the anon role: USING (share_token IS NOT NULL) - safe because the client always queries by the exact token value (.eq('share_token', token)), so this doesn't expose the whole table to anon, just whichever single row's token you already have. A new public page (e.g. shared-recipe.html?token=...) renders read-only, no auth check, no edit/delete/tag UI.

Photos are the tricky part: recipe-photos storage objects are private, gated to authenticated users (and after recipes-b28.2, to approved family members) - an anon visitor can't get a signed URL for them under that policy. Either (a) the shared view skips photos entirely (text-only recipe), or (b) generate the signed URL server-side via a small Edge Function using the service role (validates the token server-side, returns a short-lived signed URL) rather than opening photos to anon at the storage-policy level. Decide which before building - (a) is much simpler if Pete doesn't care about photos showing on shared links.

Share button itself: just needs to copy `${origin}/shared-recipe.html?token=${share_token}` to the clipboard (or use the Web Share API where available) from recipe.html.
acceptance_criteria: Clicking Share on a recipe produces a link. Opening that link in a private/incognito window (no session) shows the recipe's title, ingredients, and steps with no sign-in prompt and no edit controls. The link does not expose any other recipe.
close_reason:
Built and verified 2026-08-27, with one important design correction from the issue's original notes. The originally-proposed anon RLS policy (USING (share_token IS NOT NULL)) would have been a real security bug: RLS policies are per-row checks independent of the client's WHERE clause, so once every recipe has a non-null token, an anon client could run an UNFILTERED query and get every recipe back, not just the one matching whatever token they were actually given. Caught this before writing any code and used a SECURITY DEFINER RPC function (get_shared_recipe(p_token)) instead - anon has no direct SELECT grant/policy on recipes or profiles at all, this function is the sole narrow door, and it only ever returns the single row matching the exact token argument.

Migration 010: recipes.share_token (UUID, unique, auto-generated for every recipe via DEFAULT gen_random_uuid() - no separate 'enable sharing' step needed). New public shared-recipe.html renders a read-only view (title, byline, description, significance, meta, ingredients, steps, notes, source - no tags, no photos, no edit controls) with no auth check. recipe.html gained a Share button (any viewer, not just the owner, since any approved family member can already see the recipe) using the Web Share API where available, falling back to clipboard copy.

Verified via direct curl with only the anon key (no session at all): the RPC returns exactly one recipe for a valid token and an empty array for a bogus one; direct SELECT on recipes as anon still returns zero rows. Verified in-browser: the shared page renders correctly for a valid token, shows a clear error for an invalid one, and the Share button produces the correct link.

title: Show who added a recipe on the recipe detail page
description: At the top of recipe.html, show who added the recipe (e.g. 'Added by Peter') - only really meaningful once recipes-b28.2 (My Recipes vs All Recipes) ships, since today every recipe you can see is already your own.
design: Needs recipes.user_id joined against profiles.first_name (and/or last_name) for display. Blocker: profiles' current RLS (migration 003) only allows SELECT where id = auth.uid() - you can't read anyone else's profile row today. Needs a new SELECT policy allowing any approved authenticated user to read other profiles' first_name/last_name/avatar_url (no sensitive data lives in profiles - no email column - so a permissive read policy for authenticated+approved users is reasonable, not full public/anon access). Depends on recipes-b28.1 (admin approval) for the 'approved' gate and recipes-b28.2 for there being other users' recipes to view in the first place.
acceptance_criteria: Viewing any recipe in 'All Recipes' shows the adding family member's name near the top, before the ingredients/steps.
close_reason:
Built and verified 2026-08-27. Migration 008 opens profiles SELECT to any approved user (was owner-only), needed to look up another user's first_name/last_name for the byline - had to redefine is_approved() as SECURITY DEFINER first, since using it in profiles' own SELECT policy would otherwise self-reference infinitely (evaluating the policy calls is_approved(), which queries profiles, which re-evaluates the same policy). Kept id = auth.uid() as an explicit alternative in the new policy so a pending/rejected user can still read their own row - that's how index.html shows the waiting-for-approval message in the first place.

Found and fixed a real bug in the same pass: recipe.html's query still had .eq('user_id', userId) left over from before recipes-b28.2, so despite RLS already allowing it, you literally could not open someone else's recipe detail page - it showed 'Recipe not found'. Fixed by dropping that filter (relying on RLS) and gating the Edit/Delete buttons on an explicit isOwner check instead, so a non-owner viewing a shared recipe sees it read-only rather than a dead-end error or edit controls that would fail on save.

recipe.html now shows 'Added by <first> <last>' under the title for every recipe. Verified end-to-end: Pete's own recipe shows 'Added by Peter Morse' with Edit/Delete visible; a temporary recipe owned by Samantha correctly showed 'Added by Samantha' with Edit/Delete hidden, and was previously unreachable before this fix.

title: Redesign homepage: Google sign-in on landing, rebrand to Morse Recipes, remove separate login page
description:
Rework index.html into the single entry point for the app, replacing the current marketing-page-plus-separate-login.html flow. Four asks from Pete (2026-08-25):

1. Add the 'Sign in with Google' button directly to index.html (currently only on login.html).
2. Rename the app from 'Recipes' to 'Morse Recipes' - the page <title> and header on index.html at minimum; likely wants this applied consistently across all pages (app.html, add-recipe.html, recipe.html, profile.html, import.html, and the removed login.html's replacement) so tab titles and headers don't clash - confirm scope before implementing broadly.
3. Change the tagline/description text on index.html from the current 'Your personal recipe box.' to something about sharing the Morse family's favorite recipes.
4. Remove login.html entirely. Signed-out visitors see the marketing copy + Google sign-in (and open question: does email+password sign-in move onto index.html too, or does Google become the only sign-in method? Pete didn't say to drop email+password, but 'remove the sign in page' + 'adds Google sign-in to the homepage' reads like Google becomes primary/only - confirm before dropping email+password entirely, some users may still want it as a fallback). Signed-in visitors see 'Welcome, <name>!' (from profiles.first_name via the existing ensureProfile() logic, falling back to email if no name set) with a sign-out option.
design: Open question to confirm with Pete before/during implementation: does the signed-in 'Welcome, <name>!' state on index.html also need a way into the actual recipe list (link to app.html), or does index.html effectively become app.html (i.e. do the two merge)? Defaulting to: welcome message + sign out + a link into 'Your recipes' (app.html), keeping app.html as the actual recipe list/search page, unless told otherwise. Google sign-in wiring (signInWithOAuth, ensureProfile()) already exists and works (recipes-022.1, closed) - this issue is about moving/adding that UI to index.html and building the signed-in-state view, not building OAuth from scratch. Every other page currently redirects unauthenticated users to login.html (requireSession() pattern) - if login.html is removed, requireSession()'s redirect target needs to change to index.html (or wherever the sign-in UI lives) across add-recipe.html, recipe.html, profile.html, import.html, app.html.
acceptance_criteria: Visiting the site signed out shows 'Morse Recipes' branding, the new family-sharing description, and a working Google sign-in button - no separate /login.html page exists (or it redirects to index.html). Visiting while signed in shows 'Welcome, <name>!' with a sign-out control. All other pages' auth redirects still work correctly with login.html gone.
close_reason: Built and verified end-to-end (2026-08-25). Went with the defaults noted on the issue: 'Morse Recipes' branding applied site-wide (all page titles/headers), Google becomes the only sign-in method (email+password dropped along with login.html), and the signed-in homepage keeps a link into 'Your recipes' (app.html) alongside the welcome message and sign-out. login.html deleted; every page's requireSession() now redirects to index.html instead. index.html gained its own ensureProfile() (same logic as app.html) since it's now the OAuth landing target and needs first_name immediately for the welcome message. Verified: signed-out homepage shows new branding/tagline/Google button; signed-in shows 'Welcome, Peter!' (pulled correctly from Google metadata, backfilled into profiles.first_name/avatar_url); all 5 other pages (app/add-recipe/recipe/profile/import) redirect unauthenticated visits to index.html with no 404s; authenticated pages still work normally.

title: Better search: by ingredient, and category vs. tag
description: Current search (app.html) only matches recipe title, client-side, against whatever's already loaded. Tag filter chips exist and work but are the only 'category' concept today. Pete asked for 'a way to search recipes and categories' - need to decide whether categories are a new distinct concept (a single required grouping per recipe, e.g. cuisine or meal type) layered on top of the existing free-form multi-tag system, or whether tags already cover it and search just needs to get better (e.g. matching ingredients, not just title).
design: At minimum: extend app.html's search to also match against ingredient names (currently only recipes.title, loaded client-side - ingredients are already fetched-able from the JSONB column, or could use a Postgres full-text/GIN index for server-side search once the recipe count grows past what's comfortable to filter client-side). Open question for Pete before building: does 'categories' mean introduce a distinct single-select category field (e.g. Breakfast/Dinner/Dessert) separate from the existing multi-tag system, or is tagging already the intended category mechanism and this is just about search quality? Confirm before implementing the schema change.
acceptance_criteria: Typing an ingredient name (not just a title word) into search surfaces matching recipes. Categories/tags are filterable and it's clear from the UI which concept (tags vs. a new category field) is in play.

title: Finished-dish photos on a recipe (multiple, each with a description)
description: Let the user attach photo(s) of how the finished dish actually turned out, separate from the source recipe photos captured during AI import. Distinguishes 'photo of the source I extracted this from' (import feature) from 'photo of what I made'.
design:
Resolved 2026-08-27 (Pete): finished-dish photos are a list, not a single hero photo, and each photo carries its own description - answering this issue's original open question in favor of "a lightweight media table" over reusing the unused recipes.photo_path column.

Schema: new table recipe_photos (id UUID PK, recipe_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES recipes(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, storage_path TEXT NOT NULL, description TEXT, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()). RLS scoped via recipe_id IN (SELECT id FROM recipes WHERE user_id = auth.uid()) for all operations, with is_approved() gating INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE (same pattern as recipes-b28.1's gate on recipes/tags/recipe_tags).

recipes.photo_path (migration 001, still unused) should probably be dropped once this ships, rather than left as a second, redundant single-photo concept alongside the new list.

Storage: reuse the existing recipe-photos bucket (migration 002's {user_id}/... RLS already covers this), new path convention {user_id}/finished/{recipe_id}/{uuid}-{filename}, parallel to import.html's existing {user_id}/imports/... path.

UI: an upload control on recipe.html (simpler than add-recipe.html, since these are added after the fact once you've actually cooked the dish, not during initial recipe entry) - file picker, optional description text input per photo, uploads straight to storage + inserts a recipe_photos row. Recipe detail view shows the photo grid with each photo's description (e.g. as a caption below/overlaid on the thumbnail), plus a way to delete an individual photo.
acceptance_criteria: From a recipe's detail page, can upload one or more photos of the finished dish, each with an optional description entered at upload time. All photos display on the recipe detail view with their descriptions. Each photo can be deleted individually without affecting the others.
close_reason:
Built and verified 2026-08-30. Migration 011 adds recipe_photos (id, recipe_id, storage_path, description, created_at) - updated the design from this issue's older notes (written before recipes-b28.2 shipped) to match the now-shared-visibility model: SELECT is approval-gated like recipes/tags/recipe_tags (any approved family member can see finished-dish photos on any recipe), while INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE stay scoped to the recipe's owner only.

recipe.html: new 'Finished Dish Photos' section between Steps and Notes, showing a photo grid with each photo's description as a caption. Recipe owners get an upload control (file + optional description, same image-resize-before-upload helper as import.html) and a Delete button per photo; non-owners see the grid read-only. Storage path convention {user_id}/finished/{recipe_id}/{uuid}-{filename}, reusing the existing recipe-photos bucket.

Verified end-to-end via the actual upload/insert/render/delete code paths (not just direct table checks): uploaded a real test photo with a description, confirmed it rendered correctly in the grid with its caption and a working signed URL, clicked Delete, confirmed both the recipe_photos row and the storage object were actually gone afterward (not just hidden client-side).

title: Google sign-in for Recipes
description: Add Google OAuth sign-in alongside the existing email+password flow, mirroring Houstory's login.html (houstory-96t.11) and Five Wonders' pattern. Currently login.html/add-recipe flow is email+password only, requiring Admin-API confirmation for new signups since email confirmation is on by default.
design: Mirror Houstory: sb.auth.signInWithOAuth({provider:'google', options:{redirectTo: origin+'/app.html'}}). Requires enabling the Google provider in the Supabase dashboard (Auth > Providers) for project hhkxmuxcmjzvpjvctgqk and configuring OAuth consent/client in Google Cloud Console - this is a manual dashboard step, not just code. On first Google sign-in, ensureProfile() should seed profiles.first_name/last_name/avatar_url from user_metadata (given_name/family_name/picture), same as Houstory's app.html ensureProfile().
acceptance_criteria: Sign-in page shows a 'Sign in with Google' button; clicking it completes OAuth and lands on app.html with a session; profiles row is created/backfilled from Google metadata; existing email+password sign-in still works unchanged.
notes: Decision 2026-08-25: separate/new Google OAuth client for Recipes, not reusing Houstory's. Code is done and pushed (login.html Google button + signInWithOAuth, app.html ensureProfile()). Blocked on Pete completing two manual steps outside CLI/agent reach: (1) create the OAuth client in Google Cloud Console with redirect URI https://hhkxmuxcmjzvpjvctgqk.supabase.co/auth/v1/callback, (2) enable the Google provider + paste client id/secret in the Supabase dashboard (Authentication > Providers) for project hhkxmuxcmjzvpjvctgqk. Once done, verify end-to-end in browser before closing.
close_reason: Verified 2026-08-25: Sign in with Google button correctly redirects to Google's real OAuth consent screen (accounts.google.com, 'continue to hhkxmuxcmjzvpjvctgqk.supabase.co', no client/config errors) after Pete configured the Google Cloud OAuth client, enabled the provider in Supabase, and fixed Site URL/Redirect URLs (was defaulting to localhost:3000, causing the post-login bounce to localhost). Could not complete the actual login myself (needs Pete's real Google credentials) - Pete to do one real sign-in to confirm the final landing on app.html works, but everything up to that point is confirmed working.

title: Show uploader's name on recipe browse/search cards
description: recipe.html already shows 'Added by <name>' on the detail page (recipes-b28.3). Add the same attribution to app.html's browse cards (My Recipes / All Recipes list), so you don't have to open a recipe just to see whose it is - especially useful once All Recipes has photos from recipes-ddd making the list feel more like a shared family board.
design: loadData() in app.html (~line 128-142) currently doesn't fetch profiles at all. Needs a batch query for the distinct set of user_id values among the currently-loaded recipes (sb.from('profiles').select('id, first_name, last_name').in('id', [...uniqueUserIds])) - one query for the whole list, not one per card, same batching principle as recipes-ddd's thumbnail query. render() (~line 81-100) then adds a small byline under the title, same 'Added by <name>' phrasing as recipe.html for consistency, falling back to 'a family member' if the profile has no name (matches recipe.html's existing fallback).
acceptance_criteria: Every recipe card in both My Recipes and All Recipes shows who added it, matching the phrasing already used on the recipe detail page. No extra per-card network requests - one batched profiles lookup for the whole visible list.

title: Move Share button to top of recipe page, use standard share icon
description: The Share button on recipe.html (recipes-b28.4) currently sits near the bottom, styled as a plain text button ('Share') next to Edit/Delete. Move it to the top of the page near the title, and give it the standard share icon instead of/alongside the text label - Pete pointed at Five Wonders' existing share buttons as the reference to match.
design:
Five Wonders precedent (github.com/docneville/five-wonders, list-detail.html): uses this exact SVG for its share icon everywhere (the list-detail share button AND the place-sheet share button both use it) - a box with an arrow pointing up out of it, the standard iOS/generic 'export/share' glyph:

<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2.2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M4 12v8a2 2 0 002 2h12a2 2 0 002-2v-8"/><polyline points="16 6 12 2 8 6"/><line x1="12" y1="2" x2="12" y2="15"/></svg>

Five Wonders places it as a small pill/icon button (.ld-share-btn: rounded-pill background, 16x16 icon, icon+label) directly in the header area next to the title (.ld-actions), not down by other page actions - that's the placement pattern to match too, not just the icon.

For Recipes' recipe.html: move the button from its current spot (near Edit/Delete at the bottom, recipe.html ~line 47-49) up into the title/byline area near the top of the card. The existing click handler (Web Share API with clipboard-copy fallback, already built for recipes-b28.4) doesn't need to change, just the button's markup/icon and its position in the page.
acceptance_criteria: The Share button appears near the top of the recipe detail page (by the title), using the same share icon Five Wonders uses, not plain text. Clicking it still works exactly as before (native share sheet or clipboard copy).
close_reason: Built and verified 2026-08-27. Moved the Share button from the bottom (next to Edit/Delete) to a flex row alongside the title at the top of the card. Replaced the plain-text button with Five Wonders' exact share icon (box-with-upward-arrow SVG) plus label, styled as a rounded pill (.rc-share-btn) matching Five Wonders' list-detail share button pattern, using Recipes' own color tokens. Explicitly set .rc-share-btn:hover to avoid the same stuck-hover-on-tap bug fixed in recipes-oey, since it's a <button> that would otherwise inherit the global accent-dark hover. Click behavior unchanged (same Web Share API / clipboard-copy handler). Verified in browser: button renders with icon near the title, click still produces the correct share URL.

title: Allow selecting multiple tag filters at once
description: Tag filter chips on app.html only support one active tag at a time (clicking a second chip replaces the first instead of adding to the selection). Pete wants multi-select - e.g. filter by 'dinner' AND 'quick' together, or however many tags at once.
design:
Current state (app.html): activeTagId is a single value (~line 44), renderTagFilter()'s click handler does activeTagId = activeTagId === id ? null : id (~line 110-121, toggles between one id and null - selecting a second chip clobbers the first), and render()'s filter check is r.tagIds.has(activeTagId) (~line 59).

Change activeTagId (singular) to an activeTagIds Set: clicking a chip adds/removes it from the set instead of replacing it; each chip's .active class is driven by activeTagIds.has(t.id); render()'s matchesTag check needs to combine multiple selected tags.

Open question to confirm before building: when multiple tags are selected, should matching recipes have ALL of them (AND - narrows results, e.g. 'dinner' + 'quick' only shows quick dinners) or ANY of them (OR - broadens results, e.g. shows anything tagged dinner OR quick)? Most tag-filter UIs of this kind (narrowing down a list) default to AND; recommend that unless Pete wants OR instead. Either way, the empty-selection case (no tags active) should keep showing everything, same as today.
acceptance_criteria: Tapping multiple tag chips selects all of them at once (each shown green/active), and the recipe list narrows to match the combination per whichever AND/OR semantics gets chosen. Tapping an active chip again deselects just that one tag, leaving the others active. Deselecting all tags shows the full list again.

title: Tag filter chip stays green after tapping to deselect
description: Tapping an active (green) tag filter chip on app.html to deselect it should turn it back to its default white/outline style, but it stays green after the tap.
design:
Verified the JS toggle logic (app.html ~line 110-121) is correct: activeTagId properly clears to null on a second click, renderTagFilter() re-renders with no .active class on any chip. This is a CSS issue, not a state bug. .rc-tag-chip (recipes.css ~line 171-179) has no :hover rule of its own, so it falls through to the global button:hover { background: var(--rc-accent-dark); } (recipes.css ~line 103-105) - accent-dark is a similar green to --rc-accent, so a hover-triggered chip looks the same as an active one. On touch devices there's no mouse to move away and clear :hover after a tap, so the hover state sticks visually on the just-tapped chip until the user taps elsewhere - reading as 'it stayed green' even though .active correctly cleared underneath.

Fix: add an explicit .rc-tag-chip:hover rule (e.g. background: var(--rc-bg) to match its default look, or no change at all) so it stops inheriting the generic button:hover green, and make sure .rc-tag-chip.active:hover still reads as active (e.g. background: var(--rc-accent-dark) only for the active+hover combination, not plain hover). Consider whether other buttons in the app have the same stuck-hover-on-tap problem on mobile (e.g. wrapping hover effects in @media (hover: hover) app-wide would fix it everywhere at once) but this issue is scoped to just the tag chips.
acceptance_criteria: On a touch device, tapping an active tag chip to deselect it immediately shows the default white/outline style, not green - no lingering hover tint. Tapping to select still shows green immediately.
close_reason:
Fixed and verified 2026-08-27. Added .rc-tag-chip:hover { background: var(--rc-bg); } so an inactive chip no longer falls through to the global button:hover accent-dark green, plus an explicit .rc-tag-chip.active:hover { background: var(--rc-accent); } so the active chip unambiguously stays accent-colored under hover too (rather than relying on source-order specificity ties between .active and :hover, which have equal specificity).

Verified with a genuine CSS :hover test (the computer tool's hover action, which drives the real browser pointer rather than simulating events) rather than just reasoning about the CSS: hovering an inactive chip now resolves to rgb(250, 248, 243) (--rc-bg) instead of the old accent-dark; hovering the active chip stays rgb(122, 140, 74) (--rc-accent). This is exactly the mechanism behind the reported bug - on touch devices :hover persists after a tap (no mouse to leave with), so a just-deselected chip kept showing the hover-triggered accent-dark green until a later tap elsewhere cleared it, even though the underlying .active class had already correctly cleared.

title: Hamburger menu for site navigation
description: Add a hamburger menu for navigation, replacing/supplementing the current bare text-link nav in each page's <header> (e.g. app.html's 'Profile | Sign out', recipe.html's single 'Your recipes' link). Especially relevant on mobile once the nav grows to include My/All Recipes, Add Recipe, Import from Photo, Profile, Sign out, and (if built) Admin approval - too many links to keep bare in a header.
design: A slide-out or dropdown panel with: Home, My Recipes, All Recipes (once recipes-b28.2 ships), Add Recipe, Import from Photo, Profile, Admin (if recipes-b28.1 gets an in-app admin UI and viewer is_admin), Sign out. Same as breadcrumbs (recipes-b28.5), this touches every page's header - build as a shared markup/script pattern copy-pasted per page (matching the app's no-framework convention) rather than one-off per page, and consider doing both nav issues in the same pass since they're visually adjacent (breadcrumb trail below a hamburger-opened header).
acceptance_criteria: Every page has a hamburger icon that opens a menu listing the site's main sections, correctly reflecting signed-in state (no Sign out / Profile when signed out) and admin status if applicable. Works on mobile viewport widths.
close_reason: Shared nav.js injects a hamburger button + slide-out panel into every page's header (Home, Your Recipes, +Add Recipe, Import from Photo, Profile, Sign out), with active-page highlighting, replacing the old scattered header nav links. Menu adapts to signed-in state via the page's own sb client. Verified: opens/closes correctly, active item highlighted, sign-out from the menu works, no horizontal overflow at 375px mobile width.

title: Breadcrumb navigation
description: Add breadcrumbs to pages for easier navigation (e.g. Home > Your Recipes > Grandma's Roast Chicken > Edit). Currently every page just has a single 'back' style link (e.g. 'Your recipes' on app.html/recipe.html/etc.) - no real trail.
design: Natural trails per page: index.html (root, no breadcrumb) > app.html ('Your Recipes' or 'All Recipes' depending on recipes-b28.2's toggle) > recipe.html (recipe title) > add-recipe.html (either 'Add Recipe' hanging off Your Recipes, or 'Edit' hanging off the specific recipe when editing an existing one) > import.html ('Import from Photo' hanging off Your Recipes). Best built as a small shared helper (a renderBreadcrumbs(items) function) copy-pasted per page like the rest of the app's shared patterns (no build step/framework), or a tiny included <script src="breadcrumbs.js">. Worth sequencing alongside or after recipes-b28.6 (hamburger menu) since both touch every page's header layout - doing them together avoids restyling the header twice.
acceptance_criteria: Every page except the homepage shows a breadcrumb trail back to Home, with each ancestor level clickable.
close_reason: Built as part of the shared nav.js (recipes-b28.6). Every page except index.html shows a breadcrumb trail (Home > Your Recipes > ... > current page/recipe title), each ancestor clickable. recipe.html's breadcrumb updates live once the recipe title loads. Verified end-to-end in browser across app/recipe/add-recipe/import/profile.html, no console errors.
